LESSON: MUSICAL RHYMES

Grade: PP1
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMANCE
Topic 9.1: musical Rhymes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about musical Rhymes. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recite simple rhymes for 5 Lessons
2. demonstrate the ability to recite simple rhymes for fun
3. Appreciate different rhymes composed rhymes

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. recite simple rhymes for 5 Lessons
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to recite simple rhymes for 5 Lessons. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. demonstrate the ability to recite simple rhymes for fun
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate the ability to recite simple rhymes for fun. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. Appreciate different rhymes composed rhymes
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate different rhymes composed rhymes. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about musical Rhymes.
2. Explain musical Rhymes to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: Guide learners in groups to 1. Which rhyme do you Rhymes learner should be able to; listen to recorded rhymes recite? a) recite simple rhymes for
4. Show that you can: recite simple rhymes for 5 Lessons
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about musical Rhymes. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is musical Rhymes important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Guide learners in groups to 1. Which rhyme do you Rhymes learner should be able to; listen to recorded rhymes recite? a) recite simple rhymes for
2. Guide learners to listen 2. Whose rhyme do you 5 Lessons enjoyment specialists demonstrate like most? b) demonstrate the ability to recite rhyming simple rhymes for fun
3. Guide learners to rhyme in c) Appreciate different rhymes pairs or small groups
4. Environmental, language, Mathematics Invite a specialist to demonstrate different rhymes Non-formal activity to support learning Suggested Assessment
5. Guide learners to perform 1. Which singing games games leaner should be able to; singing games freely. do you enjoy most? a) Identify simple singing games

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. recite simple rhymes for 5 Lessons
2. demonstrate the ability to recite simple rhymes for fun
3. Appreciate different rhymes composed rhymes

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
